root_cause.text: The BPF array map clearing path in `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` iterated over all `max_entries` and invoked expensive `PROG_ARRAY` deletion/poke work (`__fd_array_map_delete_elem()`/`prog_array_map_poke_run()`) without any rescheduling point, allowing a workqueue thread to run too long and trigger an RCU stall.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cond_resched()` inside the `for` loop in `kernel/bpf/arraymap.c`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that for large `PROG_ARRAY` maps the loop calls `prog_array_map_poke_run()` per entry and “without yielding this can cause RCU stalls under load,” with the stack trace showing `bpf_fd_array_map_clear` -> `__fd_array_map_delete_elem` -> `prog_array_map_poke_run`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add cond_resched() to the BPF fd array map clear loop so large map deletions can yield CPU time and avoid long scheduling stalls.
intent_record.what: The loop in bpf_fd_array_map_clear() was changed from a single-statement for-loop to a braced block, and a call to cond_resched() was added after each __fd_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i, need_defer) invocation.
intent_record.how: During clearing of a BPF fd array map, the function now periodically yields the CPU between element deletions when needed, reducing the chance of long uninterruptible execution and improving scheduler responsiveness for large maps.

grouping_result.intent: Add cond_resched() to the BPF fd array map clear loop so large map deletions can yield CPU time and avoid long scheduling stalls.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding a rescheduling point in the BPF fd array map clear loop, preventing long-running deletion/poke work from monopolizing a workqueue thread and causing RCU stalls.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates over all max_entries without any rescheduling point, creating the long-running execution window that can stall a workqueue thread.
This per-entry deletion call performs the expensive PROG_ARRAY deletion/poke work on every iteration, and when executed repeatedly in the unbroken loop contributes directly to the RCU stall.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop walks all map entries during clear without any rescheduling point. In large maps, repeatedly executing the expensive per-entry deletion work in one uninterrupted workqueue context can monopolize CPU time long enough to trigger an RCU stall.

This per-iteration deletion call performs the costly fd/prog array removal work. When invoked for every entry inside the unbroken max_entries loop, it is the expensive operation that makes the clear path long-running and causes the scheduling stall.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant clearing logic is fully shown in this snippet. The function `bpf_prog_array_map_clear()` performs `for (i = 0; i < array->map.max_entries; i++) prog_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i);` with no rescheduling point inside the loop. This matches the root cause: iterating over all `max_entries` and invoking per-entry deletion work without yielding. The delete path `prog_array_map_delete_elem()` does nontrivial work via `old_prog = xchg(array->prog + index, NULL); if (old_prog) { bpf_prog_put(old_prog); ... }`, so the clear path can repeatedly do expensive per-entry work. There is no `cond_resched()`, batching, or other mechanism in `bpf_prog_array_map_clear()` to prevent a long-running worker/thread from stalling. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant clearing path and the fix directly. The vulnerable root cause was that map-free clearing used the normal delete path with deferred expensive PROG_ARRAY cleanup, causing long workqueue execution while iterating all `max_entries` without rescheduling. In this commit, `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` is changed from `static void bpf_fd_array_map_clear(struct bpf_map *map)` to `static void bpf_fd_array_map_clear(struct bpf_map *map, bool need_defer)`, and inside the loop it now calls `__fd_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i, need_defer)` instead of always calling `fd_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i)`. The new helper `__fd_array_map_delete_elem(..., bool need_defer)` passes that flag to `map->ops->map_fd_put_ptr(map, old_ptr, need_defer);`, while the old public delete wrapper still uses `true` for normal deletion: `return __fd_array_map_delete_elem(map, key, true);`. Crucially, the map-free paths now call clear with `false`: `perf_event_fd_array_map_free()` uses `bpf_fd_array_map_clear(map, false);`, `cgroup_fd_array_free()` uses `bpf_fd_array_map_clear(map, false);`, and `array_of_map_free()` uses `bpf_fd_array_map_clear(map, false);`. This shows the expensive deferred deletion behavior is no longer used during map free, which is exactly the fix described by the commit message. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is present.
